title: Identifier origin resolution requires convergent immutable evidence
purpose: Prevent repository materialization, search hits, completion prose, or namespace collisions from being promoted into historical origin claims for M-004, M-005, or M-006.

observed: The active queue requires exhaustive branch inventory or equivalent history traversal before M-004, M-005, or M-006 may be classified as unlocated.
CM-1019 separates repository_materialization_event from origin_event and records verified materialization anchors while retaining unresolved origin status.
CM-1020 demonstrates that negative repository code search is coverage-ambiguous and cannot prove absence.
The specialist registry contains no continuity-mining specialists and permits changes only after a durable evidenced capability gap is recorded.
inferred: Origin resolution is a multi-predicate identity problem rather than a single-search retrieval problem.

A candidate can be immutable and temporally early yet still fail because it documents later materialization, references an existing identifier, belongs to another namespace, or lacks explicit assignment semantics.
proposed: Evaluate every origin candidate through the required predicates in origin_acceptance_contract before changing origin_status.
Retain candidate-specific rejection reasons so later evidence can replace only the failed predicate rather than rewriting the entire provenance history.
Use origin_status=unlocated only after a retained exhaustive coverage manifest closes every accepted search domain without unresolved tool or provider limits.
superseded: Treating first repository appearance as identifier assignment.
Treating zero search results as exhaustive absence.
Treating automation completion prose as an immutable provenance object.
Treating suffix or label similarity across unrelated namespaces as identity agreement.
unresolved: The origin_event for M-004 remains unresolved.
The origin_event for M-005 remains unresolved.
The origin_event for M-006 remains unresolved.
An exhaustive inventory of accessible refs and reachable commits has not been retained.
The originating decision log, language lexicon, project document, or approved chat-history source that assigned the identifiers has not been located.

required_predicates.requirement: The candidate is addressable by an immutable commit, blob, retained file hash, or approved immutable source locator.
The candidate explicitly assigns the disputed identifier rather than merely mentioning, importing, reconciling, or materializing it.
The identifier belongs to the same continuity namespace; suffix or token equality alone is insufficient.
The assigning actor or artifact authority matches the continuity system responsible for the identifier.
The candidate assigns the same semantic role later attributed to the identifier.
The assignment predates all verified repository materialization anchors and later reconciliation records.
At least one independent provenance edge agrees on identifier, event type, and semantic role, or the assigning object is self-authenticating under an approved decision-log rule.
No unresolved collision, competing assignment, source-coverage gap, or tool-limit ambiguity remains material to the conclusion.

origin_acceptance_contract.promotion_rule: origin_status may become verified only when every required predicate passes. A failed or unknown predicate preserves origin_status=unresolved.
origin_acceptance_contract.unlocated_rule: origin_status may become unlocated only when exhaustive coverage is retained and every inspected candidate fails with recorded reasons; incomplete coverage preserves unresolved.
origin_acceptance_contract.materialization_rule: A repository_materialization_event may bound the search interval but never satisfies explicit_assignment by itself.

falsification_routes: Produce an immutable object that explicitly assigns M-004, M-005, or M-006 and passes every required predicate.
Show that a required predicate rejects a known valid origin under the repository truth hierarchy, then revise only that predicate with retained counterevidence.
Complete an independently reproducible exhaustive traversal and demonstrate that the unlocated_rule is either too weak or too strong.
Demonstrate that CM-1019 or CM-1020 misstates the immutable objects or search outcomes on which this contract depends.
